tool_input.body:
Release-prep. The v4.18.0 release requires a clean working tree, and these had accumulated uncommitted during the cluster-2 sessions.

## What this is

Contracts, results, reflections, and delegation records for the three missions run during the cluster-2 bug work:

- **`m-2026-09-08-001`** — cluster-2 storage layer model (DES-075), shipped in #508
- **`m-2026-09-08-003`** — dispatch binding; closed **escalated** on a leader scoping error, where the contract asked for work its own write-set excluded
- **`m-2026-09-08-004`** — the re-scoped disclaim work, shipped in #509

Committing these is the intended behavior, not cleanup: sealed audit records are the git-blame mechanism for agent work (DES-058). Their accumulating uncommitted during long sessions is known friction, tracked as `ethos-gtqq`.

## One thing worth recording

The commit surfaced this:

```
warning: session e1e5a0da... wrote mission-log lines for mission m-2026-09-08-003
but its mission live log is gone; unsealed mission-log lines were lost
```

Same for `m-2026-09-08-004`. Those sessions ran in a git worktree that was removed at the end of the session, taking their not-yet-sealed live logs with them.

That is a live instance of **`ethos-015a`** — *"removing a git worktree with an active session loses unsealed audit lines"* — observed rather than theorized. The sealed history in this PR is intact; what was lost is the unsealed tail of two missions' event logs. Worth attaching to that bead as a real reproduction, since it happened through the ordinary path: work in a worktree, finish, let the worktree be cleaned up.

The warning itself did its job — it named the session, the mission, and what was lost, which is how I noticed at all.

## Verification

Docs/state-only; no runnable code touched, so Phase 3 verification is N/A. The pre-commit `ethos audit seal` hook ran and sealed this session's chunks as part of the commit.

tool_input.body:
Accurate observation, already disclosed in the record itself, and deliberately not being changed.

The result's own `open_questions` states the omission and its reason verbatim:

> Rounds 8 and 10 edited `internal/audit/paths.go`, `internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`, and `internal/hook/audit_vacuum_test.go`, which sit **OUTSIDE** this contract's declared `write_set`. […] **Declared here rather than omitted; they are absent from `files_changed` above only because the result schema requires every declared path to fall inside the `write_set`.**

So the two fields disagree because the schema forces them to. `ethos mission result` validates that every `files_changed` path falls inside the contract's `write_set` and rejects the submission otherwise. Files edited outside it cannot be declared there — the only place left to record them is prose, which is what happened.

**Two reasons not to "fix" this.**

It is a **historical audit record**. Editing a submitted result to make its fields agree would falsify the record of what was actually submitted, in a repo whose product is that record. The disagreement is evidence, not noise.

And the real defect it points at is upstream and already recorded: I scoped that contract's `write_set` to exclude files the work necessarily needed, twice on this bead. The predecessor mission `m-2026-09-08-003` was closed **escalated** for exactly that, with a reflection naming it a leader scoping error. The right fix is better write-sets at dispatch time, not reconciled fields after the fact.

What your finding does surface as genuinely worth changing: the schema offers no sanctioned way to record an out-of-write-set edit, so the honest answer lands in free text where nothing can check it. That is a real gap in the mission result schema. Filing it separately rather than editing history here.

Declining — the rule exists but does not apply here, and I checked its scope rather than assuming either way.

The only em-dash rule in this org's instruction set is in `.docs/AWS.md`, under AWS Guidance:

> Do not use em dashes in AWS resource names or descriptions. Use hyphens instead.

That is scoped to **AWS resource names and descriptions**, where the constraint is about naming conventions in cloud resources. It is not a repo-wide prose ban, and there is no other em-dash rule in the global, workspace, or repo `CLAUDE.md`. These are mission audit records — prompts, success criteria, and explanatory prose — not AWS resources.

Independently of scope: these are **historical audit records of text that was actually written and submitted**. Rewriting punctuation inside a sealed mission record would change the record of what was said, in a repository whose product is that record. Even a genuinely applicable style rule would not justify retro-editing an audit trail; it would justify changing what gets written going forward.

Worth stating for the next reviewer, since this file will keep growing and the same flag will recur: `.punt-labs/ethos/missions.jsonl` and everything under `.punt-labs/ethos/missions/` are append-only historical records. Style findings against them should be read as findings against the *authoring* conventions, not as edits to make in place.

When work legitimately edits a file outside the write_set — which happens when the leader scoped the write_set wrong, or when a review finding cites a file the contract did not anticipate — there is no sanctioned field to record it.

The honest answer lands in open_questions as free prose, where nothing validates it, nothing indexes it, and a reader comparing files_changed against open_questions sees two fields that disagree.

OBSERVED on m-2026-09-08-001 (cluster-2 storage layer): files_changed lists 11 in-write-set paths; open_questions states that rounds 8 and 10 also edited internal/audit/paths.go, internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go, and internal/hook/audit_vacuum_test.go, and explains they are 'absent from files_changed above only because the result schema requires every declared path to fall inside the write_set.'

A qodo review on PR #511 flagged the disagreement as a correctness bug in the record. It is not — the record is accurate and self-disclosing — but the reviewer had no way to tell that from the schema, which is the actual problem.

- An out_of_write_set_changes field parallel to files_changed, same path/added/removed shape, explicitly permitted to fall outside the write_set and requiring a justification string per entry. Keeps files_changed's invariant intact while making the exception first-class and checkable.

Either way the leader should see out-of-set edits at reflect time, since they are usually evidence the write_set was scoped wrong — which is the upstream defect. On this bead the predecessor mission m-2026-09-08-003 was closed escalated for exactly that, and m-2026-09-08-004 hit it again.

tool_input.commit_message:
Contracts, results, reflections, and delegation records for the three missions run during the cluster-2 bug work:

- m-2026-09-08-001 — cluster-2 storage layer model (DES-075), shipped in #508
- m-2026-09-08-003 — dispatch binding, closed escalated on a leader scoping error
- m-2026-09-08-004 — the re-scoped disclaim work, shipped in #509

Committing these is intended, not cleanup: sealed audit records are the git-blame mechanism for agent work (DES-058). Their accumulating uncommitted during long sessions is known friction (ethos-gtqq), and a clean tree is required for the v4.18.0 release.

The commit surfaced a live instance of ethos-015a: two missions' unsealed live logs were lost when the worktree that produced them was removed. Sealed history is intact; the warning named the session, mission, and what was lost.

Review findings, both declined with reasoning rather than by editing history:
- Em dashes in audit prose: the only em-dash rule in this org is scoped to AWS resource names and descriptions, not prose. Independently, retro-editing punctuation in a sealed record falsifies the record.
- files_changed omitting three out-of-write-set paths: accurate and already disclosed in the result's own open_questions. The schema forbids declaring paths outside the write_set, so the honest answer had nowhere structured to go. Filed as ethos-p0xu.
